41.description: Saskatoon recognized Anna Fairbairn as the 2025 Budz-Guenter Memorial Scholarship recipient. She is a University of Saskatchewan biomedical sciences student whose father serves with the Saskatoon Fire Department.

47.description: The committee recommends the city administration proceed with detailed design for an overpass at the 8th Street and Canadian Pacific Kansas City rail crossing. This aims to separate road and rail traffic.

chips.text: Commuters and residents using 8th Street will be affected.

48.description: The committee recommends repealing the helicopter services policy and updating the policy for flypasts and parachute jumps to streamline city approvals.

chips.text: Organizations and individuals seeking city approval for aerial activities.

46.description: The committee recommended declaring $26.7 million in land development profits, allocating $4.0 million to affordable housing, $2.7 million for land acquisition, and $20.0 million for capital projects.

chips.text: Four million dollars would fund future affordable housing initiatives.

79.description: The committee recommends City Council adopt the 2026-2029 Strategic Plan, outlining the city's priorities for the next four years.

76.description: A committee recommends repealing the bylaw that established Saskatoon's crest and coat of arms, and updating the city's corporate visual identity policy.

77.description: The committee recommended City Council receive a report on travel and training expenses for council members in 2025.

78.description: City Council is recommended to receive a report about the 2025 car allowance for councillors, in line with existing policy.

50.description: The committee recommends City Council adopt procedures and appointments for various city boards, commissions, and committees for the year 2026.

64.description: The Social Services Subcommittee recommends Amber Lenius be appointed as the Ministry of Social Services representative for 2026.

65.description: The Saskatoon Accessibility Advisory Committee recommends reappointing Amanda Titman as the CNIB representative until the end of 2027.

66.description: The committee recommends reappointing Shantelle Watson as the Saskatoon Tribal Council's representative to the Meewasin Valley Authority until the end of 2026. This ensures continued Indigenous representation.

67.description: The committee recommends appointing Scott Waters to the Meewasin Valley Authority Appeal Board until the end of 2028. This board handles appeals related to development within the Meewasin Valley.

68.description: The committee is recommending that City Council appoint Mike Velonas, Steve Seiferling, and Jay Strohan to the Downtown Business Improvement District.

chips.text: New members include representatives from law, hospitality, and conservation.

69.description: The committee recommends that City Council appoint Jennifer Senger, Kole Kuiack, and Leah Hientz to the Riversdale Business Improvement District.

chips.text: Riversdale Business Improvement District would gain three new board members.

70.description: The Public Art Advisory Committee recommends appointing Nathaniel Odusola as a citizen representative until 2027 and continuing to seek a First Nations or Métis community representative.

71.description: The committee recommends the City Clerk readvertise a vacancy on the Municipal Planning Commission to ensure its full membership.

chips.text: Future applicants for the Municipal Planning Commission vacancy.

72.description: The Saskatoon Environmental Advisory Committee recommends reappointing two citizen representatives to serve through 2027.

chips.text: Angela Spence and Usman Ahmad are recommended for committee reappointment.

73.description: A committee recommends appointing Bryan McCrea and Darla Deguire to the SaskTel Centre board, with terms expiring in 2027.

chips.text: The Saskatchewan Place Association Inc. Board would gain two new members.

74.description: A committee recommends City Council instruct its representative to vote for Jay Aasen's appointment to the Remai Modern Board of Directors for a term ending in 2028.

chips.text: The Art Gallery of Saskatchewan Inc. (Remai Modern) board would gain a new member.

45.description: The City Solicitor will take action under The Tax Enforcement Act for properties with outstanding 2025 tax liens, with actual property names now listed.

chips.text: Committee requested actual property names be listed in the report.
Owners of properties with outstanding 2025 tax liens.

43.description: Saskatoon will spend $1.7 million from reserves to manage Dutch Elm Disease, which is rapidly spreading citywide. This funds tree removal, new plantings, and equipment to protect the urban canopy.

chips.text: Councillor Gipel questioned if the city was diligent in past DED management.
Saskatoon residents face significant risk to urban canopy aesthetics and shade.
City transitions to active long-term Dutch Elm Disease management model.
Long-term financial plan for Dutch Elm Disease management beyond two years remains unclear.
SOS Trees supports the budget request and strategy for Dutch Elm Disease management.
Dutch Elm Disease poses significant risk to Saskatoon's urban canopy and environmental benefits.
Administration will provide seasonal updates and a 2026 canopy assessment.

81.description: Saskatoon will acquire 130 Idylwyld Drive North for $1.635 million to establish a permanent drop-in center for people experiencing homelessness, funded federally. Up to $350,000 from the Affordable Housing Reserve will cover renovations.

chips.text: Councillor Timon highlighted the "not in my backyard" dilemma when dealing with human beings.
A new 90-space childcare center is opening across the street this spring.
Council requested a detailed budget for the $350,000 renovations, which was not yet available.
Funding renovations from the Affordable Housing Reserve is an exception to Council Policy C03-003.
It is unclear if the Riversdale and Downtown BIDs consistently receive safety reports.
A speaker flagged potential liability risks due to the proximity of a 90-child daycare.
Administration committed to developing a coordinated safety plan with neighbors and businesses.

82.description: The city approved amending a lease agreement with the University of Saskatchewan for vacant space in the Saskatoon Field House. This change allows the University to invest $750,000 for a rehabilitation science clinic.

chips.text: City Solicitor explained the amendment accommodates the University's $750,000 investment.

83.description: This bylaw amends a previous land re-designation for Fire Station No. 10 on a 0.34-acre site along Hunt Road in Dunl Park, by attaching a detailed subdivision plan.

chips.text: Information Services Corporation required more detail for subdivision approval.

63.description: Saskatoon will explore options for enhanced winter road services and traffic safety, including snow and ice management, around high-density residential complexes housing seniors and accessibility-challenged residents.

chips.text: Councillor Parker opposed the speed zone motion due to existing city policy.
Staff advised against lowering speed limits for traffic calming.
Residents have expressed concerns about speeding and injuries for years.
